description: The canonical Auto-Pigeon incident taxonomy. A user-impacting error path maps to one of these codes or ADDS one here; a component-local string invented at a call site is what this file exists to stop. JSON rather than TypeScript because AUB and AUE are Go, the observability tooling is Python, and three hand-maintained copies of one list is the failure mode this whole package is a reaction to.

codes.summary: A 3D redraw is still running long after the operation that triggered it.
The WebGL context was lost. Recoverable while the context comes back on its own; render.3d.fatal is the one that does not.
The 3D renderer failed unrecoverably and this editor session can no longer be trusted to draw.
A 2D viewport redraw is abnormally slow.
The 2D renderer failed unrecoverably.
The browser main thread stopped responding. Detected by the worker heartbeat, because a blocked main thread cannot paint the dialog that would report it.
A transform is still running past the stall threshold.
A transform failed part-way and the consistency of the working state is unknown.
An editor operation failed and was not applied.
auto-pigeon-backend could not be reached at all.
auto-pigeon-backend accepted the request and did not answer in time.
auto-pigeon-backend refused or failed a request.
The collaboration connection dropped and a reconnect is in progress.
Reconnection to the collaboration session did not succeed and shared working state may be behind.
A client or room is producing faster than it can be served and messages are being deferred or dropped.
The collaboration server refused or failed a message.
The extractor is not configured or has no way to run.
An extraction job exceeded its time budget.
An extraction job failed and reported a reason.
An extractor worker died without reporting a job result.
The gallery failed to load or render what was asked for.

The incident backend itself could not be reached. Reported locally and never escalated to the user: a monitor that raises a modal about its own absence is a monitor causing the outage it exists to observe.
A job the companion supervises (an owned-game tool run, an extraction hand-off) failed. Which one travels on `subsystem`; the command line, the arguments and every owned-game path stay local.
The companion could not become ready: its AUB account link, a configured backend or its own local service did not answer within its bound.

The launcher could not bring a stack up: a step, a readiness wait or a child process failed. `subsystem` names which (compose, readiness, child), `operation` names the component; the launch stopped and tore down what it had started.
